bull.b: The debt repayment materially simplifies Soluna’s capital structure, releases liens on Dorothy project assets, and reduces financing obligations. Lower leverage should improve flexibility to fund renewable-powered computing growth and advance AI projects without the same level of balance-sheet pressure.

Conditional Base Load status protects interconnection capacity in a crowded Texas queue, supporting the company’s ability to scale renewable-powered computing. This strengthens Soluna’s development position and provides a durable infrastructure advantage for future AI and high-performance workloads.

The Applied Digital joint venture expands Soluna’s AI infrastructure strategy while bringing a partner’s development capital and data-center expertise. Co-locating the project with the Briscoe Wind Farm can support Soluna’s renewable-power model and broaden its future computing revenue base.

bear.b: Deep losses, low gross margins, and substantial negative free cash flow show that Soluna has not yet demonstrated self-funded operations. Continued cash consumption can require external financing and may constrain the company’s ability to convert its expansion pipeline into durable shareholder returns.

The decline in proprietary mining revenue highlights exposure to weaker mining economics even as Soluna expands capacity. Converting capacity toward hosting may diversify operations, but the transition can reduce direct mining contribution and leaves near-term profitability dependent on successful new workloads.

The expanded share authorization gives Soluna financing flexibility, but future equity issuance could dilute existing holders while the company funds capital-intensive AI and renewable projects. Reliance on equity is particularly relevant because operating cash flow and free cash flow remain negative.
